Hi Vivek / Marissa,

We're coming up on our annual renewal and the execs want clarity on what a move to a higher throughput tier would look like vs staying on the current plan with modular credits. Two things specifically:

- If we upgrade tiers, what is the guaranteed latency/throughput delta and how does billing reflect burst vs baseline?
- If we stay and buy credits, what are the downgrade protections and how do credits roll forward (if at all)?

We're also sensitive to near-term budget timing — the CFO will want a clear path to avoid surprises, so pricing clarity + a downgrade safety net is important.

Can you share 2-3 practical packaging scenarios we can present to Tom and procurement? A one-page matrix would be ideal.

Laura — thanks for the clear ask. Quick reply with an outline, attaching a scenario CSV and a short SOW stub for the canary upgrade. I'll summarize options here and Marissa / Ben can add details: 

Option A — Tier Upgrade (Recommended for steady high throughput)
- Baseline: move to Tier 3 reserved capacity (predictable slots).
- Latency: ~20–40% median token latency improvement for your average 1k seq requests (based on our telemetry).
- Billing: flat monthly commit + metered overage. Burst capacity included up to X% per month.
- Downgrade: 90-day notice window; prorated credits applied toward downgrade balance.

Option B — Current Tier + Modular Credits
- Baseline: keep Tier 2; buy committed credits that convert to throughput units.
- Latency: no change (same service class) but flexibility for burst traffic.
- Billing: credits consumed first; unused credits expire after 12 months unless covered by a renewal amendment.
- Downgrade: immediate; credits non-refundable but can be held as account-level credit for 12 months.

Option C — Hybrid Canary (start with credits, convert to tier on signal)
- Baseline: 3-month pilot with modular credits plus a canary reservation for peak windows.
- Billing: small commit + credits; conversion option to Tier 3 with pro-rated credit offset.
- Downgrade: full safety net during pilot; conversion terms baked into SOW.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk Tom and procurement through the matrix? I've attached: SurgeonPack_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub), pricing_model_scenario.csv (scenario numbers). Ben will follow up with technical mapping.

Thanks,
Vivek

Quick technical note to support the scenarios Vivek shared: 

- For Tier Upgrade (Tier 3): we recommend enabling per-request KV caching for your top-5 intent prefixes — that drives most of the latency wins for your workload. Expect 15–25% cost reduction per effective token after cache warm-up.
- For modular credits: suggest a "burst bucket" policy with 24-hour smoothing to avoid sudden overage charges during scheduled update windows.
- Canary conversion: we'll tag pilot traffic and produce daily delta reports; credits applied to the commit on conversion will offset up to 60% of pilot consumption (see pricing_model_scenario.csv).

I've attached a small CSV with the modeled numbers — happy to run this through a 2-week traffic trace if you share a sample.

Laura / Tom / Procurement — thanks, we'll take the meeting Monday 9:30am PT and I'll present the commercial options. Quick confirmations ahead of the call: 

- Downgrade math (example): Upgrade commit billed monthly. If you downgrade mid-cycle we apply prorated credit for the unused portion of the commit toward your account credit. Example: $60k/mo commit starting July 1, downgrade Nov 1 (after 4 months) → unused future months prorated on remaining commitment; one-time conversion fee waived if downgrade is within the first 90 days. Full worked example included in the SOW appendix.
- Minimum commit for Tier 3: 1 reserved GPU pool equivalent (we'll show the numerical commit in the deck) — this is the threshold we used for the latency targets.
- Hybrid conversion cap: up to 60% of pilot credits can convert to the commit as an offset (this is contractual and shown in clause 3.2 of the SOW stub). Remaining credits either expire after 12 months or can be used for additional overage protection depending on the amendment.

I'll bring the one-page matrix and the SOW appendix to the call. If you want us to share the one-pager ahead of time, we can drop a PDF to this thread by EOD.

See you Monday — calendar invite to follow.
